Question: There are \(6\) points on a circle. What is the maximum number of distinct chords that can be obtained by joining any two points?
Solution:
Method 1: Count only new chords

Each pair of points determines one chord. Label the six points \(A,B,C,D,E,F\), and count each chord at the endpoint that comes first in this list. Point \(A\) gives \(5\) chords; \(B\) gives \(4\) new chords; \(C,D,E\) give \(3,2,1\) new chords, respectively. Every pair has exactly one first endpoint, so this counts every chord exactly once. Joining all pairs gives
\[
5+4+3+2+1=15
\]
distinct chords, which is the maximum.

Method 2: Count from both ends

A chord is determined by its two endpoints. Each of the six points can be joined to the other five, giving \(6\times5=30\) counts. Every chord is counted twice, once from each end, so joining all pairs gives
\[
\frac{6\times5}{2}=15
\]
distinct chords. Since every pair is allowed, the maximum is \(15\).
